Peptides in Enterprise, NV

D2C Peptides ships research peptides and lab supplies to Enterprise, Nevada's largest unincorporated town at 259,959 residents, from the USA and Canada.1 The NOAA station inside the town averages 82.8 days a year at or above 100 °F,23 so this page covers heat on delivery and freezer storage after it.

Shipping to Enterprise

Orders bound for Enterprise go out from the USA and Canada; the shipping policy is the one used for every order across the United States. Most residents live in single-family homes, about 78 percent in Clark County's August 2025 estimate.12 If a parcel is left at the door, bring it in promptly, for the reasons set out under heat below. Damaged deliveries are reported through returns and refunds, certificates of analysis are posted on the lab results page once available, and the contact page is there for questions.

Keeping peptides cool in Enterprise

Enterprise holds one of the valley's NOAA normals stations, LAS VEGAS WFO, whose coordinates the Census Geocoder places inside the town;3 NOAA lists it at 693.4 meters, about 2,275 feet, above sea level.13 Its 1991 to 2020 normals give July a high of 105.8 °F and a low of 79.6 °F, and January a high of 59.0 °F and a low of 37.5 °F.13 The station averages 82.8 days a year at or above 100 °F and 137.8 days at or above 90 °F, with June to August highs of 103.6 °F and 4.78 inches of precipitation a year.2

Bachem and GenScript, two peptide makers, both point to a freezer for long-term storage of freeze-dried peptides,67 and a freezer brings its own rule: avoid repeated freezing and thawing. GenScript says peptides put through freeze-thaw cycles are susceptible to degradation, and that splitting a peptide into single-use aliquots cuts both the number of cycles and the exposure to air. It also advises against opening the stock vial again and again.7 Bachem says a peptide solution that must be stored should be split into aliquots and kept frozen below -15 °C, though it does not recommend long-term storage of solutions.614

Mixed vials of approved products are a separate case: their labels say not to freeze the solution.891011 The storage guide has more on storage, and the reconstitution calculator helps size aliquots by working out a concentration.

About Enterprise

Enterprise has grown every year since 2019, from 211,761 residents in July 2019 to 259,959 in July 2025, about 23 percent in six years and 4.1 percent in the last year alone.1 The county's own August 2025 estimate is 261,749.12 The Enterprise census-designated place takes in 66.00 square miles of land, with no water area, more than Paradise (42.40) or Spring Valley (35.51), and its internal point at 36.01 N, 115.23 W lies southwest of Paradise's.15

Clark County's planning library describes two large master-planned communities in the south of the valley. Mountain's Edge, inside Enterprise in the southwest of the valley, covers about 2,500 acres, generally south of Blue Diamond Road and west of Rainbow Boulevard.16 The County Commission first approved it in September 2002, and it has been developed with about 2,150 acres of homes, 114 acres of offices, 150 acres of commercial uses and about 700 acres for parks, schools and a fire station.16 The other, Southern Highlands, covers about 2,299 acres bounded by Interstate 15 on the east, Cactus on the north, Jones on the west and Larson on the south. The County Commission approved it on November 18, 1998, with one private golf course and at most 8,500 homes.17

Enterprise has a large Asian American population: 23.0 percent of residents are non-Hispanic Asian, alongside 36.2 percent non-Hispanic White, 18.9 percent Hispanic or Latino and 10.9 percent non-Hispanic Black (ACS 2020 to 2024).18 Among adults 25 and over, 35.7 percent hold a bachelor's degree or higher, and 24.0 percent of residents were born outside the United States.19 The median age is 36.9 years.18 By industry, 23.4 percent of employed residents work in arts, entertainment, recreation, accommodation and food services and 18.7 percent in education, health care and social assistance, and the mean commute is 23.8 minutes.20

Frequently asked questions

Is Enterprise a city?

No. Enterprise is an unincorporated town of Clark County, and the largest in Nevada's 2025 certified estimates, with 259,959 residents. Only four Nevada cities are bigger: Las Vegas, Henderson, North Las Vegas and Reno.1 In place of a city council, a Town Advisory Board created by the County Commission gives input on town matters and long-term planning.4 For an order, none of this matters: Enterprise addresses ship from the USA and Canada like any other.

Which ZIP codes are in Enterprise?

ZIP code areas 89139 and 89141 lie entirely within Enterprise, and most of 89183 (94 percent of its land) and 89178 (74 percent) does too. The town also takes in parts of 89113, 89118, 89119, 89123, 89148 and 89179, per the Census Bureau's 2020 ZIP Code Tabulation Area relationship file.5 Orders to any of these codes follow the shipping policy.

With more than 80 days a year at or above 100 °F, should peptides go in the freezer?

For long-term storage of the freeze-dried powder, the makers cited here point to a freezer: Bachem gives below -15 °C and GenScript -20 °C.67 A mixed solution is different. Both makers advise against storing peptides in solution,67 and the FDA labels for EGRIFTA SV, EGRIFTA WR, ZOMACTON and a Fresenius Kabi hCG product all say not to freeze the solution after mixing.891011 For an approved product, its own label governs.
